title: marola: an open, non-profit platform for sea conditions and bathing-water quality at Brazilian beaches, built on public data
description:
marola tells you whether and when to go into the water at a beach, and why. It is a map of the beaches of Florianópolis, Rio de Janeiro and Salvador, each scored 0-100 for today and tomorrow from the sea, wind, waves, tide and the official bathing-water quality. Every number comes from public data: OpenStreetMap for the beaches, Open-Meteo for the sea and weather forecast, and the bulletins of IMA/SC, INEA (RJ) and INEMA (BA) for water quality. Anything that could put a swimmer at risk is decided by plain rules anyone can read. A language model only writes a short summary, a second automatic pass checks it against the numbers, and it never changes a score or drops an alert. When a source does not answer, marola says "no data".

marola starts from water quality because basic sanitation in Brazil is far from solved: before surfing, fishing or diving comes the question of whether the water is fit to enter. It is open source and non-profit because much of Brazil's ocean data is held privately, and the project's promise is to give everything it gathers back to everyone.

This record archives the marola umbrella: the design proposals (MIPs), the ways of working, the aggregated documentation and the pinned versions of every repository. The project is a distributed monolith, one plan with each part in its own repository: marola-app (the pipeline that joins forecast, beaches and water quality and computes the score), marola-site (the map at marola.dev), marola-oods (the Open Ocean Data Store, an open archive of beach and water history), marola-corpus (sourced notes about the sea), marola-ml (where models are trained and tested before use) and marola-devkit (the shared development tools).
